title: Valor, Point72 back General Intuition at $6B valuation as AI startup pushes into robotics
slides: Why is General Intuition worth $6 billion already?
Valor and Point72 just funded its robotics push.
The startup has no humanoid robot on sale yet.
Investors now bet on software, not hardware, first.
Watch whether their AI brain beats physical robot rivals.
thread_text:
1. Why $6 billion before a robot?

General Intuition hit a $6 billion valuation off a promise. No humanoid is on sale, so the hype is about potential, not product.

2. Valor and Point72 bet big

Their funding backs a robotics push. But the twist: they're investing in AI software first, not the physical machine.

3. Software-before-hardware play

Investors think brains beat bodies. If General Intuition's AI can control any robot, it doesn't need its own hardware to win.

4. Watch the AI brain race

The real competition is against physical robot rivals. If their brain underperforms on real tasks, the valuation could crack.

5. Test the AI-brain logic today

Ask ChatGPT to plan a robot's morning routine. If it fails simple steps, why would a $6 billion bet succeed?

instagram.caption:
A robotics startup just hit a $6 billion valuation without selling a single robot 🤖

General Intuition just raised money from Valor and Point72 to push into robotics. But the bet isn't on hardware—it's on software. The idea: if their AI brain can control any robot, they don't need to build their own body to win. That's the whole play.

For anyone building with AI: the bar isn't demo videos anymore. It's whether the brain can pass real-world tasks. If it stumbles on simple steps, the valuation cracks.

You can test the logic today: ask an AI chatbot to plan a robot's morning routine. If it fumbles the basics, what does that say about the $6 billion bet? 🧠
